notes: §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR16 lets a PERFORM in an independent segment (segment-number 50 through 99, §1985:XVI.3.2.4 GR3) have in its range "only one of the following": "a. Sections and/or paragraphs wholly contained in one or more non-independent segments." or "b. Sections and/or paragraphs wholly contained in the same independent segment as that PERFORM statement." Implemented at 85: the grammar rule sectionDefinition parses the segment-number, VisitSectionDefinition is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85, COBOL0902 from 2002), and nothing after the parser reads the number, so every segment is resident and BindPerform and EmitOutOfLinePerform run both permitted ranges like any other (probed: a THRU range over segments 10, 20 and 49, and paragraph, TIMES, VARYING and section ranges inside segment 50, all from a PERFORM in segment 50). Not implemented: the restriction. BindPerform resolves procedure-name-1 and procedure-name-2 without their segment-numbers, so a PERFORM in segment 50 that names a section of segment 60 compiles and runs with no diagnostic. kb/Work PB5084 holds the mechanism (the accepted-inert Segmentation module, docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.18) and lists the same restriction under its Segmentation twins 1985-SR-XVI.3.3.2-L2.1 and 1985-SR-XVI.3.3.2-L2.2; it does not name this rule id. The witness runs range a (a section of segment 10) and range b (a paragraph of the same segment 50).

next.reason: 1985: "A PERFORM statement that appears in an independent segment can have within its range ... only one of the following"; 2023: "No segments: GR-14.9.28.4-1 defines the range with no segment limit ("need not appear consecutively in the source element")". 2023 has no independent segments. Its PERFORM range rule sets no limit on which sections may be in a range, so the 1985 segment restriction is dropped.
